# 6. World, Areas, Puzzles and Pacing

6.1 Environment Choice The game takes place in Napoleonic-era Gothic France. The final environment is either a mansion or a castle. The choice remains PROVISIONAL because it affects scale, traversal, available exterior spaces, military facilities, walls, water access, asset burden and narrative framing.

6.2 Major-Area Model The environment contains at least 3 and no more than 5 major production areas. Named rooms are grouped into those areas; not every room becomes a separate zone. Exact adjacency, puzzle ownership and final room list will be iterated during game production. 6.3 Location Pool Current approved location pool: dining hall; concert hall; main hall; living quarters; medical ward; warehouse; garden; lord’s room/private chamber; cemetery; optional underground dungeons; castle walls if the castle setting is selected; courtyard or small plaza; and barracks. Additional supporting rooms may be added, combined or removed as production and level flow require.

6.4 Provisional Flow Logic Flow layer Current rule Hub The main hall or central public wing provides recognizable orientation and connects several locked or obstructed routes. Area progression Each major area owns at least one puzzle chain or critical objective that changes world access. Revisiting New keys, mechanisms, shortcuts or information can send the player back through earlier areas under changed werewolf pressure. Safe havens Two or three true safe havens are distributed according to traversal time and failure cost, not simply one per area. Final route The last puzzle chain opens an exit or crossing. The werewolf’s inability to swim may become the endgame constraint. Iteration Room count, adjacency, shortcuts, puzzle order and optional content remain adjustable through greybox testing.

6.5 Puzzle Design Framework The individual puzzles have not yet been crafted. The GDD therefore locks their role and quality requirements without inventing solutions. Requirement Rule Area ownership Each major area contains a puzzle chain or objective that justifies entering and learning that space. Environmental grounding Puzzle logic must fit the building’s function, period objects and architecture rather than appear as an unrelated minigame. Interruption Puzzles occur in the active world. Whether partial progress persists and how quickly the player can disengage are determined per puzzle. Threat integration The werewolf can interrupt or pressure puzzle work, but required interactions must remain possible without spending finite resources. Clarity The environment provides sufficient clues and feedback to understand the goal, valid actions and state changes. Backtracking Revisiting is allowed when it produces new information, route mastery or changed danger rather than empty repetition. No softlocks Puzzle-critical and narrative-critical items cannot be consumed as ammunition or lost permanently. v0.2 | CONCEPT / PRE-PRODUCTION | PAGE 9

6.6 Pacing and Safe-Haven Placement
- Quiet exploration and clue interpretation alternate with search pressure, direct chase, resource decisions and short recovery windows.
- Two or three true safe havens support autosaving, clue review and crafting.
- Entering a safe haven resets the werewolf to random patrol. Exit placement and patrol spawning must prevent immediate unavoidable capture or safe-room door exploitation.
- Exact travel time between saves, neutralization usefulness and resource placement depend on the final greybox and puzzle order.
